title: Continuity router and soft replacement workflow for locked model versions
creator: Priya Nair
description: Problem: Customers can pin to exact model versions for compliance or deterministic behavior. When a pinned variant is degraded (hardware outage, security patch, or model removal), we need a predictable, auditable way to keep traffic flowing while honoring version-lock constraints and minimizing customer surprise. This ticket designs and implements a continuity routing layer ("continuity router") plus a soft replacement workflow that automates region-aware substitutes, quality-preserving fallbacks, and deprecation notifications.
acceptance_criteria: Continuity router can resolve a pinned model key to an ordered list of replacement candidates given region, customer tier, and compatibility profile
Runtime can execute an automated soft replacement without client API changes when the primary pinned instance is unavailable, and observations are recorded in audit logs
Replacement decisions respect customer's pin policy (strict-lock, allow-major-patch, allow-variant) and recorded as a deterministic decision record for debugging
We publish a performance-profile delta for any selected substitute model (token latency and unit cost), surfaced to Console and incident dashboards
Rollout includes canary for 100 customers in staging, and automated rollback on quality regressions detected by prompt-set evals
design_decisions: Introduce 'continuity router' component in control plane that evaluates a rule-scored candidate set per pinned key; rules include region proximity, quantized-size compatibility, architecture compatibility, and published performance delta

Support three pin policies: 'strict' (no automatic swap), 'tolerant' (allow same-major, different-patch), 'prefer-specified-with-fallback' (default for new customers). These map to decision thresholds in the router
Replacement candidates are scored with a weighted vector: compatibility (40%), latency delta (25%), cost delta (15%), recent regression score from evals (20%)
All substitutions are recorded as an immutable 'replacement event' with reason code, candidate list, chosen variant, and deterministic hash to support reproducible replay

Deprecation windows are explicit: 'soft-deprecate' (traffic diverted via router preference weight), 'hard-deprecate' (block except for explicit approval), each with notification cadence tied to customer usage and pinned counts
implementation_notes: Add ContinuityRouter service behind control plane API: /v1/router/resolve?pin=...&region=...&policy=... returns ordered candidates and event-hash
Extend model metadata with 'compatibility profile' and 'published_performance_profile' (latency P50/P95, token-cost estimate) at version onboarding time

Runtime agents evaluate router response at request routing time. When router returns 'substitute' and customer policy allows, runtime performs pre-warm KV-cache for the substitute variant before switching traffic for that request batch
Introduce short-lived 'soft-alias' mapping in serving layer to enable gradual traffic weighting (10% increments) for soft-deprecations and replacements
Audit log entries should include customer id, pinned key, original version, chosen substitute, region, reason, and event-hash. Persist to event store and surface in Console incident view
testing_plan: Unit tests: candidate scoring, deterministic hashing, policy evaluation edge-cases
Integration tests: router + runtime on a 3-region staging cluster with synthetic failures (node drain, model eviction, kernel crash)
E2E quality test: run customer's saved prompt-sets through selected substitutes; abort promotion if regression metric > 3% for high-usage customers
Chaos test: randomly simulate regional network partition and assert continuity router triggers expected substitute selection and that audit events are generated
Performance test: measure additional latency introduced by router lookup (goal < 2ms median) and validate KV pre-warm reduces first-token penalty
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): Deploy ContinuityRouter to staging; onboard two internal beta customers with 'prefer-specified-with-fallback' policy; validate audit logs and console surfacing
Phase 2 (canary): Enable for 100 low-traffic production tenants in us-west with soft-replace only and monitor regressions for 7 days
Phase 3 (ramp): Gradually expose to all tolerant-policy tenants and enable regional substitutes. Maintain manual approval gate for strict-policy customers
Phase 4 (full): Default behavior available in Console; provide customer opt-out and documentation; start automated deprecation campaign for models with low usage
